E1.evidence: Issue #1236 (humble binaries, rclpy 3.3.12) gives reproduction steps ("Run an action server node with the `use_sim_time` parameter as `True`", "Have a node emit clock messages faster than wall clock moves (at x60)", "Call the action") and a traceback ending in `self._result_futures[bytes(goal_uuid)].set_result(result_response)` / `KeyError: b'EM$\xc6\xb3YA:\xa9\xa1_\xd1\xeb\x88\x06\x88'`; a maintainer confirmed "Yes. Throwing an exception is not a correct behavior in this scenario." (Barry-Xu-2018).

units_identified: sim clock publisher (reporter's node publishing /clock at x60)
E2.evidence: The KeyError comes from two asynchronous coroutines inside rclpy's ActionServer operating on its own `_result_futures` dictionary: "These two parts involve asynchronous operations, so to completely avoid the issue, locking (asyncio.Lock) should be added when operating on `self._result_futures`." (Barry-Xu-2018). The accelerated /clock only shortens the result_timeout in ROS time, which maintainers describe as designed behaviour ("There is a `Result caching` in action design ... it is not guaranteed that the goal result will be consistently retained even if it has not been accessed."; "If result_timeout is still set to 0, this issue might still occur."). No value, frame, unit, or name crossing a boundary is wrong; the failure is rclpy's own unhandled race and would occur with any correct clock source or action client once a goal expires before its execution completes.

E4.evidence: "The action server fails because `self._result_futures[bytes(goal_uuid)].set_result(result_response)` in the ActionServer _execute_goal method raises a `KeyError` exception" with the traceback in the issue.

ineligible_reason: internal: race inside rclpy's ActionServer between _execute_expire_goals (removing the result future when result_timeout elapses) and _execute_goal (setting the result), exposed by a short result_timeout in accelerated simulation time. The linked PR #1363 (merged into rolling 2024-10-08 as 4d7ff9720508764ecaaef9f334df29c1c07ac187) only raises the log in _execute_get_result_request from debug to warn with the text 'Sending result response for unknown or expired goal ID: {0}'; maintainers attribute the remaining behaviour to the user's result_timeout setting ("So it's the user's responsibility to set a reasonable result timeout."). The reporter's workaround was to increase result_timeout.
